# Vajb Orbit — UI & Theming Spec

**Status:** draft 2026-09-17. Final UI/theming spec, screen by screen, mapped to concrete Godot 4.7 Control node types so the coding pass is mechanical.

**Scope rules inherited from the project:** Godot 4.7.2, Forward+, window stretch mode `canvas_items`, aspect `expand`. All UI lives under a `CanvasLayer` (UI is screen-space; the game world never scales UI anchors). Layer Cake: signals travel up, calls travel down — UI emits signals, gameplay connects.

## 1. Colour Tokens

All colours are defined once as theme colours on the base `Theme` (see §6) and referenced by name everywhere. No literal hex values in scenes or scripts except inside the theme file.

| Token | Value (hex) | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `void_base` | `#07090d` | Near-black blue void — the only background for full-screen UI |
| `void_panel` | `#0b0f15` | Raised surface for panels/dialogs |
| `void_panel_raised` | `#10151d` | Hover/highlight surface on top of `void_panel` |
| `metal_dark` | `#1b2028` | Desaturated gunmetal — bevel shadow side, inactive slots |
| `metal_mid` | `#2a313c` | Gunmetal mid — default slot/panel edge fill |
| `metal_light` | `#3d4654` | Gunmetal light — bevel highlight side, enabled borders |
| `text_primary` | `#c9d1dc` | Body text, readable contrast on all `void_*` and `metal_*` |
| `text_dim` | `#6b7484` | Secondary labels, disabled text |
| `accent_danger` | `#c8471f` | Single burnt orange-red accent — damage, danger, alerts, active fire mode |
| `accent_danger_bright` | `#e8622a` | Same hue one step brighter — hover state of danger elements only |
| `accent_nav` | `#6fb8c4` | Prograde-needle cyan (§3.6, added 2026-09-20) — velocity-vector navigation read, never a glow, never a danger colour |

**Rules:**

- Exactly one accent colour (`accent_danger`). No rainbow. Success/info states are expressed with `metal_light` + `text_primary`, not green/blue.
- `accent_nav` (2026-09-20) is the single navigation-exception colour: it colours only the speedometer prograde needle (§3.6) and nothing else; it is desaturated steel-cyan so it reads as an instrument, not a glow.
- Contrast floor: `text_primary` on `void_base` ≈ 11:1; `text_dim` on `void_base` ≈ 4.0:1 (large text / labels only, never body).
- Danger is reserved: if it is not damage, an alert, or an armed weapon, it is not orange.
- Thin bevels: 1 px only. Bevels are drawn by StyleBox borders (`metal_light` top/left, `metal_dark` bottom/right), never gradients.

## 2. Theme Architecture

One base theme resource: `vajb-orbit/ui/theme/vajb_theme.tres`, assigned once on the root `Control` of every screen (and cascading to all descendants). Per-control overrides are forbidden except for one-off special cases documented in this spec.

### 2.1 Theme resource contents

The `.tres` defines, per theme type:

- **StyleBoxes** — every StyleBox is a `StyleBoxFlat` except panel chrome, which uses `NinePatchRect`-backed textures where specified (§5). All StyleBoxFlat corners use radius 0 (hard sci-fi) or 2 px max; border width 1 px (`border_width_all = 1`).
  - `panel` — bg `void_panel`, border `metal_mid`
  - `panel_raised` — bg `void_panel_raised`, border `metal_light` top/left, `metal_dark` bottom/right (the bevel)
  - `button_normal` — bg `metal_dark`, bevel border as above
  - `button_hover` — bg `metal_mid`, border `metal_light`
  - `button_pressed` — bg `void_panel_raised`, inset bevel (borders flipped: `metal_dark` top/left)
  - `button_disabled` — bg `metal_dark`, border `metal_dark`, content margin +2
  - `focus` — 1 px border `accent_danger_bright`, no bg fill, `expand_margin` 0. **Amended 2026-09-18:** the menu plate variation no longer draws this box; the station rail, dialogs, lists and tabs keep it (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §9.8 item 1)
  - `lineedit` / `lineedit_focus` — bg `void_base`, border `metal_mid` / `metal_light`
  - `slider_groove`, `slider_grabber` — groove 4 px tall bg `metal_dark` border `metal_mid`; grabber 12×12 bg `metal_light` border `text_dim`
  - `progress_bg`, `progress_fill` — bg `void_base` border `metal_mid`; fill solid `accent_danger` (see §3.3 for variant overrides)
  - `tooltip_panel` — bg `void_panel` (90 % alpha), border `metal_mid`
- **Fonts and sizes.** A single font family (fallback: Godot default; **amended 2026-09-18:** three OFL families per IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §9.8 item 2 — Oxanium titles, Rajdhani body, Saira Stencil One flavour). Font size scale via the base theme `default_font_size = 14`, with sizes registered per type: `Label` 14, `Button` 14, `LineEdit` 14, `RichTextLabel` (`normal_font_size`) 13, tooltips 13, HUD value readouts 18, screen titles 22. One `font_size_scale` factor is applied globally at runtime through `ThemeDB`/project setting `gui/theme/custom_font_size`-style scaling so a future accessibility slider changes all sizes together (no per-node `add_theme_font_size_override`).
- **Colours** — the §1 tokens registered as theme colours on the relevant types (e.g. `Label/colors/font_color = text_primary`, `font_disabled_color = text_dim`).
- **Icons** — 16×16 line icons in `text_dim` except danger icons in `accent_danger`. No multicolour icons.

### 2.2 Focus & input conventions

- Every interactive Control shows the shared `focus` stylebox on keyboard focus; `focus_mode = FOCUS_ALL` on buttons, sliders, line edits. **Amended 2026-09-18:** the menu plates are exempt — their focus cue is the tick band plus the emblem pulse (IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §9.8 item 1).
- Tab order follows visual order (containers guarantee this); no manual focus neighbours except where noted (§5 rebinding list).
- Hover states: `button_hover` + a 1 px accent border is used *only* on armed/critical buttons; regular hover keeps gunmetal. **Amendment 2026-09-17 (menu hover-glow policy, see STYLE_BIBLE §7.3):** on menu and screen-level scenes only (`main_menu.tscn`, `loading.tscn`, dialogs), button hover adds a 6 px soft Ember Glow `#E8703A` outer halo (60 % alpha, implemented as a glow underlay `Panel` behind the plate or a shader — one implementation for all buttons) plus the hover plate art's baked ember under-light. HUD controls never use the halo.

### 2.3 Scene layout convention

Every screen scene:

```
ScreenName (Control, full rect, theme = vajb_theme.tres)
└─ UILayer (CanvasLayer, layer 10)          # HUD screens only
   └─ MarginContainer (margins 12)
      └─ ... layout per section below
```

Dialogs (§5) are separate scenes instantiated under a dedicated `CanvasLayer` (layer 20) so they always stack above HUD.

## 3. In-Game HUD

Scene: `vajb-orbit/ui/hud/hud.tscn`. Root: `Control` (full rect, `mouse_filter = IGNORE`) → `CanvasLayer` (layer 10) → four zone containers.

```
HUD (Control, MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE, full rect)
└─ CanvasLayer (layer 10)
   ├─ TopLeft (MarginContainer, anchors top-left, margins 12)
   │  └─ VBoxContainer
   │     ├─ HullBlock (VBoxContainer)
   │     │  ├─ HBoxContainer (Label "HULL" + Label value "812/1000")
   │     │  └─ ProgressBar (hull)
   │     └─ ShieldBlock (VBoxContainer)
   │        ├─ HBoxContainer (Label "SHIELD" + Label value)
   │        └─ ProgressBar (shield)
   ├─ BottomLeft (MarginContainer, anchors bottom-left, margins 12)
   │  └─ VBoxContainer
   │     ├─ AmmoPanel (PanelContainer → VBoxContainer)
   │     │  ├─ Label weapon name + ammo "Laser MkII  240/300"
   │     │  └─ GridContainer 5×1 (weapon slot TextureButtons)
   │     └─ CargoToggle (TextureButton, collapsed cargo icon)
   ├─ BottomRight (MarginContainer, anchors bottom-right, margins 12)
   │  └─ MinimapPanel (PanelContainer → VBoxContainer)
   │     ├─ MinimapView (Control, custom _draw, 200×200)
   │     └─ HBoxContainer (Label sector name, TextureButton zoom +/-)
   └─ CenterOverlay (Control, anchors full, MOUSE_FILTER_IGNORE)
      ├─ TargetReticle (Control, custom _draw, follows target)
      └─ CargoPanel (PanelContainer, hidden by default, see §3.4)
```

### 3.1 Hull & shield bars

- Both are `ProgressBar`. `show_percentage = false`; custom font display in the sibling `Label` above (value as current/max).
- **Hull**: min 0, max from ship stats. Style override (the one sanctioned deviation from pure tokens): fill stylebox bg `accent_danger`; when hull fraction < 25 % the fill switches to `accent_danger_bright` and the value label turns `accent_danger_bright` (done in script, no new tokens).
- **Shield**: fill stylebox bg `metal_light` (shield is not a danger state — it regenerates; orange stays reserved). Border `metal_mid`, bg `void_base`.
- Both bars: size 260×14, `progress_bg`/`progress_fill` styleboxes from §2.1, corner radius 0.

### 3.1b Energy & fuel bars (rulings 10/14, 2026-09-20)

Amends the TopLeft `VBoxContainer`: below `ShieldBlock` sit two more blocks,
same pattern:

- **Energy**: `ProgressBar` 260×14, fill `metal_light` (the buffer is not a
  danger state — same reasoning as shield), label `ENERGY` with the
  current/max readout. Emergency Flight Mode (fuel 0): the fill turns
  `accent_danger` while the mode lasts.
- **Fuel**: fill `metal_mid`; at ≤ 15 % of max the fill and label turn
  `accent_danger`. Label `FUEL`. While fuel == 0 an `EMERGENCY FLIGHT`
  banner Label appears above the blocks in `accent_danger_bright`.
- HUD API: `set_pool(kind: StringName, value: float, maximum: float)` with
  `kind` ∈ `&"energy" | &"fuel"`; `set_emergency(active: bool)`.
- No new tokens: every colour above is an existing token role.

**Amendment 2026-09-24 (wave D7 — owner word "looks good" on the A1 sheet +
C1's finding that the bars duplicate the new dials):** the two `ProgressBar`
blocks (Energy + Fuel) and their labels **retire from the flight HUD** — the
cluster's FUEL/ENRG value dials (§3.7 Mockup v7) are the pool readouts now. The
**`EMERGENCY FLIGHT` banner stays** (fuel == 0, `accent_danger_bright`, in the
TopLeft column where the blocks were). The HUD API is unchanged:
`set_pool(kind, value, maximum)` and `set_emergency(active)` keep their frozen
§7 signatures and feed the dials. Reversal: restore the two blocks (the text
above).

### 3.2 Ammo & weapon slots

- `AmmoPanel` is a `PanelContainer` with the `panel_raised` stylebox; inner `VBoxContainer` separation 4.
- Weapon name/ammo `Label` uses size 18 readout styling; ammo turns `accent_danger` at ≤ 10 % of magazine.
- Weapon slots: `GridContainer` with 5 columns, each cell a `TextureButton` (48×48) with the four texture states from the generated art set:
  - `texture_normal` — gunmetal slot plate, weapon silhouette in `metal_light`
  - `texture_hover` — plate brightened one step (`metal_mid` plate)
  - `texture_pressed` — plate darkened to `void_panel_raised`
  - `texture_disabled` — silhouette at 40 % alpha, plate `metal_dark` (weapon not owned / on cooldown with a cooldown overlay drawn in `_draw` as a sweeping `accent_danger` wedge)
- Active weapon additionally gets a script-drawn 1 px `accent_danger` frame on top (not a fifth texture; keeps textures palette-neutral).
- Slot keys: number keys 1–5 bound in the controls settings (§4); each slot shows its number as a tiny `Label` overlay in the corner of the cell.

### 3.3 Minimap

- `MinimapPanel` (`PanelContainer`, `panel` stylebox) anchored bottom-right; 200×200 map `Control` with custom `_draw()` — dots for ships/POIs, `accent_danger` for hostiles, `text_dim` for neutral, `text_primary` for self.
- Zoom is two `TextureButton`s (16×16) in the footer `HBoxContainer`; sector name `Label` in `text_dim`.
- **Chaff ghosts (2026-09-20, engine spec §4.6):** blip kind `&"ghost"` — a
  dim `text_dim` dot that flickers (alpha 0.3–0.7 at 6 Hz) for the 3 s ghost
  window; never hostile-red, so ghosts are distinguishable at a glance.

### 3.4 Cargo panel

- Toggleable `PanelContainer` (default hidden), anchored to the right edge below the minimap: `Control` full-rect anchor right, script positions it under the minimap footer.
- Content: `GridContainer` 5 columns of 40×40 `TextureButton` cells (same texture states as §3.2, item art instead of weapons), plus an `HBoxContainer` footer: `Label` "CARGO 12/40" and a close `TextureButton` (16×16).
- Full-cargo state: footer label turns `accent_danger`.

> **Amendment 2026-10-10 (wave S39, T-170).** §3.7 retired this panel from the
> flight HUD ("all of old HUD should be gone") and left cargo with no readout;
> the owner's second playtest found the gap ("i cannot see my current cargo while
> in flight"). S39 answers it **additively** without un-retiring the old column:
> `hud.gd` builds a code-built `CargoBlock` (`_cargo_block`, `_cargo_block_value`,
> `_cargo_block_list`, `_cargo_entries()`) into the bottom-left column beside
> `CreditsBlock`, reading `PlayerProfile.cargo_items()` — the header reads
> `CARGO used/max`, one `name x qty` row per held item (empty hold reads `EMPTY`).
> `armory_panel.gd`'s ammo `SUBTITLE` gains `HOLD used/max` (`_cargo_used`,
> `_hold_capacity`), so the slots are visible while buying ammo. The retired
> `CargoPanel`/`CargoToggle` stay hidden and on `retired_widgets()` unchanged.
> **Reversal: drop the `CargoBlock` and the subtitle token.**

### 3.5 Target reticle

- `TargetReticle` is a bare `Control` with custom `_draw()`, repositioned each frame to the target's screen position (script projects world→screen via `get_viewport().get_screen_transform()` chain from the camera node).
- Drawing: corner brackets (4 × 8 px L-shapes) in `accent_danger`, 1 px, with a target-hull micro-bar (60×4 `ProgressBar`, `show_percentage = false`) underneath bracketed by a `VBoxContainer` inside the reticle `Control`. When no target: hidden.
- `mouse_filter = IGNORE` on everything in `CenterOverlay` so the reticle never eats clicks.
- **Lock channel ring (2026-09-20, engine spec §4.1):** while the lock
  channel runs, the reticle draws a thin arc around the brackets —
  Steel Highlight `#565C63`, completing clockwise over the 1.2 s; the arc
  completes to `metal_light` and stays for the lock's lifetime. HUD API:
  `set_lock_progress(progress: float)` (empty hides).

### 3.6 Radial speedometer (ruling 19, 2026-09-20)

- Anchored bottom-centre inside `BottomLeft`'s parent column (below the
  ammo panel), a 120×120 `Control` with custom `_draw()`, `mouse_filter =
  IGNORE`.
- **Dial:** 10 segments across 270° (gap at the bottom); segment `i` filled
  with `metal_mid` when `speed_ratio ≥ i/10`, the current topmost segment
  filled `accent_danger` only while `speed_ratio > 0.9` (overdrive read).
- **Prograde needle:** a 10 px cyan line from centre at the ship's actual
  velocity bearing. **The needle cyan is the HUD's one sanctioned cyan** —
  it marks the velocity vector (navigation read, not danger), mirroring the
  shield-ripple steel exception in STYLE_BIBLE §3. `#2BE8E8` is NOT used;
  the needle colour is a new HUD-only token `accent_nav` — added to §1
  tokens with this amendment (`accent_nav = #6FB8C4`, desaturated so it
  never reads as a glow).
- **Heading marker:** a 6 px white (`bone_text`) tick at the ship's facing
  bearing on the same dial.
- HUD API: `set_speedometer(ratio: float, prograde: Vector2, heading: Vector2)`
  (angles in radians, world space); hidden while docked.

**Amendment 2026-09-24 (wave D7 — owner: "I dont get why there are two compasses
that seem to work the same?"):** the **Heading marker** bullet is **retired**.
The dial draws no heading tick; heading lives once, in §3.7's compass bay
(`ui_compass_rose` + the HDG row, same `heading` feed — the §7 API survives
unchanged). `ui_gauge_face` is re-cut with an **8-tick graduated speed scale**
(longer ticks toward the top of the 270° arc, no numbers — UI_CHROME §1.7)
instead of the uniform tick ring, so the dial reads as a speed instrument and
never as a second compass. `test_engine2_hud.gd`'s §3.6 rows move exactly where
they assert the heading tick — the yardstick moves with this amendment; the
segment/needle/overdrive rows stay byte-green. Reversal: restore the 6 px
`bone_text` tick and the old face.

### 3.7 Cockpit instrument cluster (amendment 2026-09-23, wave D6 — owner's NMS-style ask)

Replaces the bare §3.6 dial with a framed instrument cluster and adds sprite
surfaces. **§3.6's contract survives byte-identical** — `set_speedometer(ratio,
prograde, heading)`, `SEGMENTS` 10, `SWEEP` 1.5π, `OVERDRIVE` 0.9, the 120×120
gauge box and every read-back (`speedometer_ratio()`, `filled_segments()`,
`overdrive_segment()`, `needle_colour()`) — only the gauge's **surface** changes:
the painted `ui_gauge_face`/`ui_gauge_needle` sprites sit under the marks, while
the segment fill, the prograde needle and the heading tick stay code-drawn in
their tokens (`metal_mid`, `accent_nav`, `text_primary`): state-driven marks are
never baked (§3.2's "keeps textures palette-neutral" precedent). The
gauge now lives inside the cluster; the dial's old bottom-centre/bottom-left
discrepancy (`hud.gd`'s own report note) is resolved **bottom-left** (the owner's
word 2026-09-23: "all in one nice looking cockpit menu at bottom left maybe").
Reversal: move the cluster to the column foot as a bare dial (§3.6 verbatim).

- **Cluster box:** 404×216 logical, framed by `ui_cockpit_frame` (nine-slice,
  64 px band on a 192×192 master — the §10 `@2x` recipe made primary, one master,
  per the D2 ruling: no size-variant families). Reversal: 340×184 compact.
- **Layout:** left bay = gauge 120×120 (box unchanged); middle bay = compass
  96×96 rose + a 3-cell `HDG` readout beneath it; right bay = five readout rows.
- **Readout rows** (right bay), label column 34 px + digits:
  `SPD` 4 cells (u/s) — **amended 2026-09-24 (owner: "in the cockpit if all
  clocks are 4 digits make the speed 4 digits as well"); was 3 cells**,
  `HULL` 4 cells (current points), `SHLD` 4 cells (current
  points), `FUEL` 3 cells + `%` cell, `ENRG` 3 cells + `%` cell. Digit cell
  20×36 logical (7-seg aspect ≈ 1:1.8), 2 px gaps, leading blanks
  (`ui_seg_blank`) not leading zeros. Row labels 12 px `text_dim` (new §6 row
  "Instrument row label"; reversal: 14 px). Reversal on hull/shield: show %.
- **Digit semantics:** SPD = `int(round(prograde.length()))` clamped 0..9999
  (**2026-09-24 owner ruling** — SPD is 4 cells like every other row, so every
  readout row is 4 cells wide; the staged 4th-digit item is pulled forward.
  Reversal: 3 cells, clamp 0..999);
  HULL/SHLD = `int(round(current))`; FUEL/ENRG = `int(round(100 × value/max))`,
  clamped 0..100. The `%` cell lights only on the FUEL/ENRG rows.
- **State colours (digits never recolour):** danger reads exactly as §3.1/§3.1b
  but as (a) the row label turning `accent_danger` (hull < 25 %:
  `accent_danger_bright`; fuel ≤ 15 %: `accent_danger`) and (b) a script-drawn
  1 px `accent_danger` frame on the row (§3.2's on-top-frame precedent). SPD overdrive
  (`ratio > 0.9`): the needle modulates `accent_danger_bright` and the SPD row
  gets the frame. Fuel == 0: the `EMERGENCY FLIGHT` banner (§3.1b) plus the FUEL
  row frame in `accent_danger_bright`.
- **Compass:** `ui_compass_rose` rotates opposite the ship's facing
  (`-heading.angle()`), a fixed `ui_compass_lubber` triangle at top; `HDG` shows
  `int(round(rad_to_deg(heading.angle())))` mapped to 0..359. No cardinal letters
  baked (UI_CHROME §1.7 no-text law); engine `Label` cardinals are staged out.
  **Amended 2026-09-24 (owner: "The compass needs values … compass has NSWE
directions"):** N/E/S/W ship as engine `Label`s at the rose rim — r **42** from
  the rose centre, positions rotating with the rose, text upright, `N` in
  `text_primary` and E/S/W in `text_dim` (the staged-out call is reversed; the
  no-baked-text law holds — they are Labels, never art).
- New HUD read-backs (the probe precedent): `cockpit()`, `compass()`,
  `compass_heading()`, `readouts() -> Dictionary {spd, hull, shield, fuel_pct,
  energy_pct}` as drawn (post-clamp ints). **No new setters** — the cluster derives
  everything from feeds §7 already carries (speed u/s from `prograde.length()`,
  heading from `heading`, pools from `set_pool()` and the hull/shield handlers).

**Amendment 2026-09-24 (wave D7 — owner review of D6: "I dont like the cockpit
background, it looks like a computer screen while we have analog clocks etc, make
sure that everything looks analog, so they are placed on a metal panel of
something like that"; "there is overlap and generaly doesnt look too pleasing to
the eye"; "all of old HUD should be gone i think"):**

- **Instrument language (see §3.9):** every cluster surface becomes a painted
  metal instrument face. `ui_readout_glass` and `ui_cockpit_frame` retire from
  the cluster (`ui_cockpit_frame` stays in service on §3.8); the backing is the
  new full painted panel **`ui_cockpit_panel`** — one master **928×512** (2× the
  box), **no nine-slice** (the D3 1041×1087-stretched-plate defect class is
  avoided by sizing the master to the pinned box). Gauge, compass and readout
  rows mount into the panel's recessed wells. Reversal: the glass readout plate
  + nine-slice frame.
- **Box (this resolves the D6 review's R1-MED-2 as one call):** outer **464×256**
  logical, painted interior **400×192**, band **32** (the §10 `@2x` recipe's
  logical half of the 64 px master band). Reversal: 404×216 (the measured 396×190
  content overflowed its 340×152 interior — that is the defect being cured); the
  340×184 compact reversal is **dead by measurement** (cannot hold the bays).
- **Bays:** left **126** (gauge 120×120 + the battery readout beneath it), middle
  **104** (compass 96×96 + the HDG row), right **156** (the five rows at 122),
  **7 px** gutters. Reversal per bay: none needed — these are the D6 numbers plus
  the battery readout in the gauge bay's measured spare height.
- **Battery readout (left bay foot; absorbs the old §3.2 ammo panel):** one
  engine `Label` line `B1 · CANNON` (12 px `text_dim`, the §3.7 row-label style;
  rack ordinal + family resolved by the same tables the ammo panel used) + one
  **`AMMO` row**: 34 px label + **4 cells** (clamp 0..9999, leading blanks,
  `ui_seg_*`) carrying the active rack's loaded rounds on the existing ammo feed
  (§7 unchanged). Reversal: no battery readout (ammo on §3.8 only).
- **Digit fit law (the overlap cure):** every `ui_seg_*` sprite is drawn
  **fill-fitted to its 20×36 logical cell** — never at master size — on a 22 px
  cell pitch (20 + 2). `test_d7_cockpit.gd` asserts the drawn glyph rects are
  pairwise disjoint and inside their row; the blind-spot class that let the
  overlap ship dies here. Reversal: none — this is a defect cure.
- **The old HUD column dies:** §3.1's crest bars, §3.2's `AmmoPanel` and §3.4's
  cargo block are **removed from the flight HUD** (HULL/SHLD live in the cluster
  rows, ammo in the battery readout, cargo + fitted modules read on §3.8). The
  §3.3 minimap and §3.5 target reticle stay. **The §7 frozen API survives
  callable** — every frozen method keeps its signature; the widgets they drove

### 3.9 Cockpit instrument language (amendment 2026-09-24, wave D7)

The owner's ruling, verbatim: "I dont like the cockpit background, it looks like
a computer screen while we have analog clocks etc, make sure that everything
looks analog, so they are placed on a metal panel of something like that." Every
cockpit-family surface obeys this language (the cluster §3.7, the battery window
§3.10, and any later instrument):

1. **Analog first.** Readouts are painted metal instrument faces: dials with
   needles, engraved compass roses, mechanical seven-segment drums (the drum
   cells are analog machinery, not screens). No glass, no screen glow, no
   holographic or CRT/LCD framing anywhere.
2. **Everything mounts on metal.** Every widget sits in a recessed well of a
   painted panel (`ui_cockpit_panel`, the §3.10 armory plates) in STYLE_BIBLE's
   painted-metal treatment: Bone/Panel-Steel palette, ember `#C8461B`/`#E8703A`
   only for danger. Bolt/rivet heads echo `ui_cockpit_frame`'s corners.
3. **No baked text.** Engraved scales are tick marks only (UI_CHROME §1.7);
   words and numbers are engine `Label`s or `ui_seg_*` cells.
4. **State is code-drawn.** Fills, needles, ticks and danger frames stay
   code-drawn in theme tokens over the painted faces (§3.2's palette-neutral
   textures precedent). Digits themselves never recolour.
5. **Everything is user-modifiable** (owner 2026-09-24: "make sure that it is
   easily modified by the user in the future, like different styles, layout
   etc"): every colour, layout metric and asset path these surfaces use lives in
   one **`CockpitStyle`** Resource (`vajb-orbit/ui/hud/cockpit_style.gd`,
   `class_name CockpitStyle`) with `@export` groups **palette** (panel/metal/
   bone/dim/ember tokens), **layout** (box, band, bay widths + gutters, row
   pitch, label zone, drum cell size, dial radii, lamp size) and **assets**
   (panel/face/plate texture paths). Defaults = this spec's numbers, shipped as
   the built-in default; dropping in `res://ui/hud/cockpit_style_user.tres`
   overrides everything with **no code edit** (surfaces load it if present).
   Reversal: hardcoded tokens (the D6 status quo).

Reversal: the D6 `ui_readout_glass` glass look (recorded in §3.7's amendment).

**Amendment 5 (2026-09-26, owner-ruled after the S20 live playtest — the ARMORY
chrome composition; A4.1/A4.2's per-surface mapping is amended here).** Owner,
verbatim: *"look how clean auction and shipyard are done i want all to look this
clean"* and *"we always should use anchors and relative positioning"* — his
reason, *"when i dispatch each agent it generates different outcome"*. **This is
a mechanism amendment**: it fixes how a surface is built so two workers on the
same brief cannot diverge, and it fixes the chrome that the measured art cannot
honour. AUCTION/SHIPYARD are the yardstick (`auction_panel.gd:752-800` — rows are
`Button`s with container children; `shipyard_panel.tscn:74-115` — the one framed
surface is `PanelContainer`+`PanelRaised`+`MarginContainer`).

- **A5.1 Chrome is chosen by the asset's own cut size — and inside a pane it is flat.**
  The two clean panes are the yardstick: AUCTION has **no framed surface** in its
  body at all (rows are `Button`s over the theme's plates), and SHIPYARD's only
  frame is its outer `PreviewFrame`. So the ARMORY's inner surfaces (the bays, the
  well halves, the pack rows, the inventory rows) wear the flat Tokens language —
  `StyleBoxFlat`, 1 px `metal_mid` border, the theme's own `_flat()`
  (`build_theme.gd:450-457`) — and the pane's only frame is the **module host's
  own `PanelRaised`**, already the pane's outer edge. `ui_panel_frame` (96×96, a
  **32 px** band, `build_theme.gd:504-514`) is a pane-scale asset and is no longer
  drawn inside this console: at bay size it leaves a 196×128 opening for 240 px of
  cells, and at card size (68 px tall) it leaves 4 px. A code-drawn mark stays
  inside its own child rect. Reversal: A4.1's per-surface frame assignment (the
  measured overlap defects return).
- **A5.2 Composition law (the owner's rule, as mechanism).** (i) Layout is
  containers + anchors + `custom_minimum_size` + size flags — never coordinates;
  (ii) a surface's chrome is a theme stylebox or a sibling node, never a `_draw`
  pass over content; (iii) a code-drawn mark draws **within its own child rect**,
  anchored to it; (iv) chrome that carries a visual band also sets the
  `content_margin_*` that keeps content off it. A worker who needs coordinates for
  anything that must sit inside art is out of contract. Reversal: the S18/S20
  hand-derived rect layout.
- **A5.3 The measured cure (what this wave ships):** bays, well halves, pack cards
  and inventory rows wear the flat Tokens box (`bay_bg`/`item_bg` + the 1 px
  `metal_mid` border); the cells keep the machined recess (`cell_bg` + the two
  edge tones) and draw the family's `ui_slot_weapon_*` plate **at its own 48×48**
  centred (never stretched over a 117×52 cell — the S20 smear); the `✕` chip is
  pinned at its laid-out size (24×29 — the `StationButton` plate's own minimum,
  **L236** closed as accepted); A3's geometry numbers all stand (nothing moves).
  Reversal: the frame on bays/wells/cards and the stretched slot plate (the
  overlapped look).
- **A5.4 The per-surface chrome table (D14, 2026-09-26 — surface → asset/stylebox →
  content inset, every inset measured from the asset's real cut size).** The law
  this table implements, in the owner's words: **containers + anchors, never
  coordinates; no chrome drawn over content** (A5.2's four clauses, mechanism
  unchanged). Rule (Q1): a banded asset may dress a surface only when the surface's
  *ruled content* sits at least the asset's patch margin inside it — measured, the
  `ui_panel_frame` band is **32 px** (cut 96×96, `texture_margin_*` 32 + 1 px
  expand, `build_theme.gd:504-514`), so only pane-scale surfaces qualify; anything
  whose content margin is smaller wears the flat Tokens box (`_flat()`, 1 px
  `metal_mid`, `build_theme.gd:450-457`).

  | Surface | Size @ base (A3) | Chrome: asset / stylebox | Content inset, from the cut |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | Pane outer edge (module host) | host 1392×610 + `HostMargin` 20 | `ui_panel_frame` as `PanelRaised` (96×96, band 32 + 1 expand) | **36/88/36/46** — `HostMargin` 20 + console inset (16, 68, 16, 26) clears the 33 px band (≥4 px, measured); the inset is carried by the **containers**, not `content_margin_*` — registering 32 on the stylebox would move the host rect (452,214)+1392×610 → (464,226)+1368×586 = every A3 number = HIGH |
  | Console floor | 1360×516 | none — `ConsolePlate` is a `NinePatchRect` with `texture = null` (`armory_panel.gd:879`, the retired master); the host frame is the pane's edge | n/a (no chrome to clear) |
  | Bay card | 260×192 | flat Tokens box `bay_bg` + 1 px `metal_mid` | **10** (`cell_margin`); head **34**, ledge **240×34 @ y150**, foot **8** — unchanged A3 |
  | Bay cell | 117×52 | machined recess (`cell_bg` + 2 edge tones) + `ui_slot_weapon_*` drawn **1:1 at 48×48** centred as a mark (cut 48×48, silhouette x8–47 y0–34 → never stretched) | text **6** (name x6, width cell−24); the 48×48 plate sits behind the text at the cell centre (34.5, 2) |
  | Salvo ledge | 240×34 | flat Tokens box `ledge_bg` + 1 px | **10** from the bay edge (`ledge_rect` = bay−`cell_margin`); segs `ui_seg_*` (cut 48×88) drawn **18×32** on a 20 pitch, caption 13 px beside |
  | Well half | 648×220 | flat Tokens box + 1 px; caption on the 20 px band gap **above** the box | **0** — the grid fills the half exactly (2×320+8 = 648; 3×68+2×8 = 220); a 32 px band here would put the outer cards under the metal (why the frame is refused) |

## 4. Settings

Scene: `vajb-orbit/ui/screens/settings.tscn`. Root `Control` full-rect, bg `void_base` drawn by a full-rect `PanelContainer` with the `panel` stylebox (or `ColorRect` with `void_base` as first child — spec choice: `PanelContainer` for consistency).

```
Settings (Control, full rect)
├─ PanelContainer (full rect, stylebox panel)
│  └─ MarginContainer (margins 24)
│     └─ VBoxContainer
│        ├─ HBoxContainer (header)
│        │  ├─ Label "SETTINGS" (size 22)
│        │  └─ spacer (Control, EXPAND)
│        │  └─ Button "BACK"
│        ├─ TabContainer (EXPAND_FILL both axes)
│        │  ├─ Graphics (VBoxContainer)   # tab title "GRAPHICS"
│        │  ├─ Audio (VBoxContainer)
│        │  ├─ Controls (VBoxContainer)
│        │  └─ ...
│        └─ (TabContainer owns the bottom edge; no footer bar)
```

Tab titles: "GRAPHICS", "AUDIO", "CONTROLS", "INTERFACE" (interface reserved for HUD scale/opacity toggles later).

### 4.1 Graphics tab

`VBoxContainer` of setting rows; each row is an `HBoxContainer` (label left, control right, separation 16):

- Resolution — `OptionButton` (listed for completeness; `OptionButton` is a themed `Button` subclass, uses the same styleboxes)
- Display mode — `OptionButton` (windowed / fullscreen / borderless)
- V-Sync — `CheckButton`
- Render scale — `HSlider` (0.5–2.0, step 0.05) + `Label` value readout
- Shadow quality / effects quality — `OptionButton`

### 4.2 Audio tab

Same row pattern:

- Master / Music / SFX / UI volume — four `HSlider`s (0.0–1.0, step 0.01) each with a `Label` percentage. Sliders bind to audio bus volumes via `AudioServer`.

### 4.3 Controls tab — key rebinding list

```
Controls (VBoxContainer)
├─ ScrollContainer (EXPAND_FILL vertical)
│  └─ VBoxContainer (rebind rows)
│     └─ RebindRow (HBoxContainer, per action)
│        ├─ Label action name ("THRUST FORWARD")
│        ├─ spacer
│        ├─ Button key binding ("W")     # opens listen-mode
│        ├─ Button alt binding ("▲")
│        └─ Button reset ("↺")           # 24×24 TextureButton alternative
└─ HBoxContainer (footer)
   ├─ Button "RESET ALL"
   └─ spacer
   └─ Button "SAVE"
```

- Bind buttons are `Button` (not TextureButton) — text shows the current key; pressed state enters **listen mode**: the button text changes to "PRESS KEY…", next `InputEventKey`/`InputEventJoypadButton` captured via `_input`, conflicts highlight both rows' labels in `accent_danger`.
- Focus neighbours: within a row, left/right arrows walk binding buttons; `ui_up/ui_down` walk rows — the `ScrollContainer` scrolls the focused row into view (`ensure_control_visible`).
- Joypad bindings use the same buttons; event display string comes from a shared `InputEvent → display name` helper.
- Rebind rows are created from the project's action list at runtime (data-driven; the scene ships one template row).

## 5. Tooltips, Dialogs & Nine-Patch Panels

### 5.1 Tooltips

- Custom tooltip scene `tooltip.tscn`: root `PanelContainer` with `tooltip_panel` stylebox → `RichTextLabel` (`bbcode_enabled = true`, `fit_content = true`, width capped at 320 px via custom minimum size x).
- Attached via `Control.set_tooltip` replacement: a small autoload/helper that instantiates the tooltip scene and positions it offset (12, 12) from the mouse, clamped to the viewport, on `mouse_entered` with a 0.25 s delay (script-driven; Godot's default `get_tooltip()` path is bypassed because default tooltips are not themeable enough).
- Content grammar (BBCode): item name line in `text_primary` bold, stats in `text_dim`, danger warnings in `[color=#c8471f]`. Tooltip text sources come from item `Resource` data (`Resource` pattern — tooltip_string property), never hardcoded in scenes.
- Item tooltips (equipment/hangar, §5.3) additionally include the slot-type line and drag hint ("DRAG TO EQUIP").

### 5.2 Dialogs (confirm / message)

Scene: `dialog.tscn` (modal confirm/prompt, used for rebinding conflicts, selling confirmation, reset-all):

```
DialogRoot (Control, full rect, MOUSE_FILTER_STOP)     # blocks input behind it
├─ ColorRect (full rect, void_base at 60 % alpha)      # dimmer
└─ CenterContainer (full rect)
   └─ PanelContainer (min size 420×0, stylebox panel_raised)
      └─ MarginContainer (margins 16)
         └─ VBoxContainer (separation 12)
            ├─ Label title (size 18)
            ├─ Label body (autowrap, text_primary)
            └─ HBoxContainer (alignment END, separation 8)
               ├─ Button "CANCEL"
               └─ Button "CONFIRM" (danger styling: normal stylebox border accent_danger)
```

- Instantiated under `CanvasLayer` layer 20. Only one dialog at a time; the helper autoload queues requests.
- Dialogs grab focus on open (`CONFIRM` default focus) so Escape/Enter work; Escape maps to CANCEL.

### 5.3 NinePatchRect panels (hangar/equipment chrome)

The hangar and equipment screens use a textured metal-frame chrome for the main panels (bevelled plates with riveted corners — generated art), implemented as `NinePatchRect`:

- Scene `metal_panel.tscn`: `NinePatchRect` with `patch_margin_*` values baked from the source texture's frame thickness. Baseline for the generated frame texture (32 px frame in a 96×96 source): `patch_margin_left/top/right/bottom = 32`. Coding pass must confirm the actual frame width from the final texture and set all four margins to it; if the texture ships a 16 px frame, margins become 16.
- Usage: as the visual background **behind** a `PanelContainer` whose `panel` stylebox is set to a transparent `StyleBoxEmpty` — the NinePatchRect provides pixels, the PanelContainer provides layout:

```
SlotPanel (PanelContainer, stylebox_override = StyleBoxEmpty)
├─ NinePatchRect (full rect, metal frame texture, patch margins = frame width)
└─ MarginContainer (margins 24)   # content inset inside the frame
   └─ ... slot grid / list
```

- Same pattern for the dialog chrome variant (optional swap for `panel_raised`).

### 5.4 Equipment & Hangar screens

Scene: `vajb-orbit/ui/screens/hangar.tscn` (equipment is a tab/panel of hangar; single screen, two views).

```
Hangar (Control, full rect)
├─ PanelContainer (full rect, panel stylebox)         # screen background
└─ MarginContainer (margins 16)
   └─ HBoxContainer (separation 16)
      ├─ LeftColumn (VBoxContainer, EXPAND_FILL)
      │  ├─ HBoxContainer header (Label "HANGAR" / "EQUIPMENT" + credits Label)
      │  └─ ViewSwitch (HBoxContainer, two TextureButtons: HANGAR / EQUIPMENT)
      ├─ ShipPreview (Control, custom _draw of ship silhouette + equipment overlay anchors)
      │  └─ HardpointMarkers (8 × Control, positioned by data; each holds a 40×40 TextureButton slot)
      └─ RightColumn (VBoxContainer, min width 380)
         └─ MetalPanel (PanelContainer + NinePatchRect per §5.3)
            └─ MarginContainer (16)
               └─ VBoxContainer
                  ├─ HBoxContainer (filter OptionButton + search LineEdit)
                  ├─ SlotGrid (ScrollContainer → GridContainer 6 columns)
                  │  └─ ItemSlot (TextureButton 56×56) × N
                  └─ Footer (HBoxContainer: selected item stats RichTextLabel + action Buttons)
```

- **Slot grids**: `GridContainer` columns = 6 (hangar inventory) / 5 (equipment hardpoints as a grid alternative view). Each `ItemSlot` is a `TextureButton` (56×56) with the §3.2 texture states; equipped-state adds a script-drawn `accent_danger` corner triangle (armed/relevant accent only when the item is a weapon being compared).
- **Drag & drop** (hints + implementation notes for the coding pass):
  - Slots set `texture_disabled`-style dimming when a drag from an incompatible slot type hovers over them (drag preview via `Control.get_drag_data()` returning `{ "type": "item", "id": ... }` + a `set_drag_preview(TextureRect)` of the item icon at 50 % alpha).
  - `can_drop_data()` validates slot type + level; on invalid, the slot draws a 1 px `accent_danger` border (script `_draw` on hover) — this is the only sanctioned use of orange outside danger semantics, because a failed drop *is* a warning state.
  - `drop_data()` emits `item_moved(from_slot, to_slot)` up to the hangar controller (signals up).
  - Keyboard fallback: focus a slot, press Enter to "pick up", Enter on another slot to place — mirrors drag; documented in the tooltip hint line.
- **Hangar ship list** (left column, when in HANGAR view): `ItemList` (themed via `panel` + `item_selected` styles) or a `VBoxContainer` of custom rows — spec choice: `VBoxContainer` of rows for full theming control; rows are `Button`s with `alignment = LEFT`.

catalogue** (measured 2026-10-03) — the module is new content pinned as

## 10. The map deck and the navigation pin — design detail (amendment 2026-10-03, wave D18 — D18-A1)

§9's N1–N6 are the law; this section is the wireframe-grade detail S29 codes
against (mockup: `staging/mockup/d18_map_deck_wireframe.md`). Composition is
A5.1–A5.4 throughout; no new art (owner 2026-09-27). Presentation values new
in this block carry their reversal and tick id below — the **N** rows continue
§9's series at N7; nothing above is renumbered.

**Deck composition (N1/N2).** One `PanelContainer` (A5.4 `Pane outer edge`,
`ui_panel_frame`, ASSET_CATALOG.md:444) centred at 80 % of the viewport. Its
body is one `HBoxContainer`: the map viewport (a `Control` that expands; the
compact map's own blip classes and drawing law move up into it —
`minimap.gd`) beside the filter column at `custom_minimum_size (240, 0)`
(**PROPOSED**; reversal `(180, 0)`). The deck's foot is the A5.4-3 caption
strip carrying the zoom read, the hint line and the spool/cooldown/arrival
reads (§A2 of the mockup). Toggle paths: **M**, the compact map's corner
EXPAND button (a 36×36 `TextureButton` beside the shipped `ZoomMinus`/
`ZoomPlus`, `hud.tscn:409-431`), and **ESC** (N1's three routes). Pan/zoom:
LMB drag pans — a press only counts as a drag past an **8 px** threshold
(**N14**); wheel zooms 25 %–400 % centred on the cursor; arrow keys pan in
64 px steps (N2's numbers).

**The filter column (N3).** A `VBoxContainer` of toggle rows, each the A5.4-2
service-strip idiom (base `Button` bevel + a `StationValue` label — the
auction tab plate idiom, `auction_panel.gd:113,361-362`): the N3 label with a
trailing `ON`/`OFF` state read (`text_primary`/`text_dim` — label + state,
never colour alone). The eight toggles persist per profile through the
existing `PlayerProfile` save (`user://profile.cfg`, 01 §7). **N6's exemption
lands on the classes that draw STATION and GATE blips** — `KIND_STATION`/
`KIND_GATE` (**N15**/**N16** below, PROPOSED): those two classes are drawn on
deck and compact map whatever the filters say, and until they ship nothing on
either map is exempt (N6 filters nothing today). `KIND_SELF` carries no toggle
and is never filterable. **The toggle→blip-class mapping** (`minimap.gd:141`
names the shipped five — `KIND_SELF`, `KIND_HOSTILE`, `KIND_FRIENDLY`,
`KIND_SWARMER`, `KIND_GHOST`):

| Toggle | Rides |
|---|---|
| STATIONS | `KIND_STATION` — new class (**N15**) |
| GATES | `KIND_GATE` — new class (**N16**) |
| ASTEROID FIELDS | `KIND_ASTEROID_FIELD` — new class (**N17**) |
| POIS | `KIND_POI` — new class (**N18**); the shipped `KIND_GHOST` also rides this toggle (**N19**) |
| HOSTILES | the shipped `KIND_HOSTILE` (N3's own row); the shipped `KIND_SWARMER` also rides this toggle (**N20**) |
| FRIENDLY | the shipped `KIND_FRIENDLY` (N3's own row) |
| CARGO & WRECKS | `KIND_WRECK` — new class (**N21**) |
| CONTRACTS | `KIND_CONTRACT` — new class (**N22**) |

**The navigation pin (N4).** Press-down **hit-tests the pin first**: a press
that hits the pin is a **remove candidate and never a place or move** (a short
press on it removes the pin — `cancel_orders`, `player_ship.gd:426`); a press
that misses the pin places or moves the one destination pin, and its release
< 0.5 s issues the **existing** autopilot order (`set_move_target`,
`player_ship.gd:419`) to the pin — one action, one press; any stick input
cancels the order (`player_ship.gd:816`). Hold ≥ 0.5 s (N5 fitted) jumps —
armed from press-down, on a fresh pin and on the existing pin alike. **The pin
is placed at press-down and does not follow the cursor**: it is set at the
press point and stays there; a held move past N14's 8 px threshold is a pan
(N2), not a pin move, and the pan leaves the pin where it was placed. Pin
reads: the diamond mark is a code-drawn
mark in its own child rect (A5.2(iii)) in `text_primary` at 6 px — friendly
blips are 3 px (`minimap.gd` FRIENDLY_RADIUS) — **PROPOSED**, reversal

**The owner's words (2026-10-03, the shell-v2 ruling):** "the containers dont
sit in the same place when hovering between different sections. First the select
menu where i select 'auction' 'refinery' etc has to be gone but only the visual
aspect, not the functionality. i want it to slide from left of the screen when
you press a Menu button (come up with something) and also i want new pane: space
station overwiew (where you will be able to press on shipyard on move to
shipyard instead of using menu) Lets remove the bottom panel with description it
occupies way too much space. instead of it lets make a popup when you hover on
something? or add 'inspect' button. if we inspect a module make a screen popup
as well, it was bo be responsive menu." Tone and budget (same day): "i want the
screen to look grimdarky but operate smoothly. if new sprites are needed then
there are credits on kie.ai to use." The five open points were ruled by the
owner's tick answers the same day: **both** hover tooltip and INSPECT modal;
OVERVIEW carries tiles + identity + ship + services + flavour (**all five**);
OVERVIEW is the **landing pane on dock**; the drawer button is **TERMINAL**;
both instability defects are live (cross-pane misalignment **and**
hover-induced movement).

Mechanism facts already measured: the band is `ui/screens/station.tscn:214`
(`Inspector`, `InspectorTitle`/`InspectorBody` `station.gd:150-151`) and dies
with this wave (STATION_HUB §18's supersession block); the hover→describe chain
survives (`inspect_requested`, `station.gd:518`, `tests/test_s11_inspector.gd`)
and only its sink changes; the hover-induced movement is measured at
`ui/station/shipyard_panel.gd:703-733` (`HoverStatBlock` — an in-flow `Label`
inserted mid-stack in `_stats`, visibility-toggled with rewrapping text on every
cell hover) with its fitting twin (`fitting_panel.gd`, same formatter); the
cross-pane misalignment is per-pane skeleton drift (scene `custom_minimum_size`
counts 1–10 across `ui/station/*.tscn`, zero `offset_` placements — A5 holds at
scene level, the divergence is in what each pane's skeleton declares). The
tooltip idiom (§5.1) and the modal idiom (§5.2) are law and unimplemented in
`ui/` today. Wireframe-grade detail is `UI_SPEC.md` §12 (wave D19).

### 12.5 A5.5 operationally — the test, the reserved slot, the defect census

**The test (N31).** A handler violates A5.5 when a hover / focus / selection
**state change** mutates any node's size or `custom_minimum_size`, its position
or offsets, an in-flow node's `visible`, or the node tree (add, remove,
`move_child`, reorder). Legal on the same events: colour, `modulate`, `_draw` /
`queue_redraw`, theme state swaps (stylebox/texture states), and in-place content
swaps (text, texture) inside a pinned box. A user **command** — press, drop,
filter-tab press, expander press, pane switch, overlay open/close — is not state
feedback and may rebuild and show/hide content (the auction filter tabs' shipped
row filtering, `auction_panel.gd:403-408`, is the pinned precedent). A
`ScrollContainer` may auto-reveal the focused row (a viewport offset, never a
node's position); hover never scrolls.

**The reserved slot (N24's "one fixed reserved slot per pane"):** the foot band's
hint cell (STATION_HUB §19.3), fixed at **18 px** — one `StationCaption` line
box inside the 56 px band, width-reserved so a content swap cannot reflow the
band. It is the one place hover-revealed content may live in-flow (the
`· CANDIDATE` fit preview, `armory_panel.gd:3767-3768`); multi-line hover
content is N27/N28's. Reversal is N24's own: a taller slot reinstated at a
stated height.

**The census** — every hover/focus/selection handler under `vajb-orbit/ui/` at
write time. Cure classes: **DELETE → TOOLTIP** (the in-flow content dies; its
bytes ship in the N27 tooltip) / **RESERVED SLOT** (pin the slot so a content
swap cannot reflow) / **RETROFIT** (swap the violating mechanism for
colour/`modulate`/`_draw`, look unchanged) / **ALREADY LEGAL** (no cure). S30
cures the shell rows from this table alone; menu/HUD rows are named for
completeness and ride their own screens.

| # | Site | Trigger | Mutation | Verdict | Cure |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `ui/station/shipyard_panel.gd:703-733` (`_mount/_refresh/_clear_hover_block`) | cell hover (`:549-550`, `:853-859`) | `HoverStatBlock` `add_child` + `move_child` mid-`_stats` (`:713-714`); autowrap `text` + `visible` per hover (`:726-727`, `:733`) | violation (node tree + in-flow `visible` + reflowing text) | **DELETE → TOOLTIP** (N30) |
| 2 | `ui/station/fitting_panel.gd:1469-1491` (`_mount/_refresh_stat_block` — the fitting twin) | row/sub-row hover + focus (`:852-853`, `:924-925`, `:1200-1215`) | `StatBlock` `add_child` + `move_child` into `_footer` (`:1476-1477`); `text` + `visible` (`:1490-1491`) | violation (the same defect) | **DELETE → TOOLTIP** (N30) |
| 3 | `ui/station/shipyard_panel.gd:957-988` (`_refresh_preview` / `_update_preview_size`) | selection (`_on_row_focused` `:1029-1035` → `_preview_row` `:1105-1110`) | `_preview_image.custom_minimum_size` (`:962`, `:988`) | violation (size on selection) | **RESERVED SLOT** — the `PreviewFrame` keeps one pinned box (§3.1's preview row); the ship scales inside it |
| 4 | `ui/station/armory_panel.gd:3755,3768` (`_refresh_footer` `:3122-3127`) + `ui/station/fitting_panel.gd:1192,1210` | browser-row hover/focus | the foot meter's `text` swap (`· CANDIDATE` preview) in an auto-width label | violation risk (foot-band reflow) | **RESERVED SLOT** — the 18 px hint cell above, width-reserved |

## 13. The D20 fix wave — exchange parity, the armory browser, the hover-inspect popup (amendment 2026-10-04, owner's playtest notes 1–3; wave S31)

Owner notes verbatim (`slices/D20-station-playtest/D20_synthesis.md` §0):
note 1 — "make the 'your hold' in exchange look the same and make sure that
they are even = on same height" (the same = the marker board); note 2 — "in
armory the 'modules owned and buyable' shifts out of screen"; note 3 — "inspect
time twice as long on hover, make it a bit clearer maybe to read?". Ticks
**T-124–T-126 decided at the owner's go 2026-10-04** (defaults taken: the
linger reading, two full-screen modes, regroup + readout). Measured facts these
pins build on (D20-P1/P2, 1920×1080): hold RowBox 474 px inside the 500 px box
(icon 40 + cells 70/80/100 + the 96×32 chip + 6×12 separations leave the title
28 px), board title 517 px, the hold's header band off its own columns by
96+12 px, the lists starting 26 px apart, armory row inner 542–620 px in a
478 px row / 490 px `BrowserScroll`, `TOOLTIP_DELAY := 0.25`, tooltip body
`text_dim` at 13 px in a 320 px cap.

### 13.1 The pins (N42–N47)

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|
| **N42** | both EXCHANGE lists render **one shared row builder** (the board's praised plate: 76 px row, icon 40, expand-fill title, meta line, value columns) and **one AUCTION-idiom column-header band** per list (§5.10's row: caption cells seated exactly over their value columns, values right-aligned). The captions are the row stacks' own words — hold `UNITS · CR EACH · CR NET`, board `INDEX · BAND · QUOTA`; the per-row caption stacks and `CAPTION_HELD`/`CAPTION_VALUE` are deleted (S28-A12's band superseded) | S28-A12's hold-only band + the per-row caption stacks as shipped |
| **N43** | the hold title column never renders below **180 px**: value columns rebalance to ≤ 60/64/80. The per-row `INSPECT` chip and the trade-column cluster chip are retired (N37 rev 2026-10-07): the header's one INSPECT toggle opens the sheet. Only if a row still starves the title may the hold box widen **500 → 560** (board 876 → 816) | the per-row chip + 70/80/100 + the 500 box |
| **N44** | both lists' scroll viewports begin on **one y** (identical caption → header → scroll stacks) and the outer boxes stay even at 635 px | the hold-only band's 26 px offset |
| **N45** | the armory browser row trims its title to a fixed **160 px ellipsis column** (port `exchange_panel.gd`'s trimming `_make_label`) and the browser half widens **490 → 620** (split 1262/490 → 1132/620). Acceptance: every row control lands inside the 1920×1080 window | untrimmed titles + the 490 half (the shipped overflow) |
| **N46** | the hover-inspect popup **lingers 0.5 s after the pointer leaves** (2× `TOOLTIP_DELAY` — T-124's A reading, the owner's "twice as long") and holds steady while the pointer crosses a row's children (re-arms only when the hovered row/cluster changes) | no linger; re-arm per child enter/exit |
| **N47** | the tooltip body renders `text_primary` (not bold; the INSPECT hint stays `text_dim`) and its `RichTextLabel` font is **15 px scoped to the tooltip node** (never the theme default), cap width **320 → 360** | the dim body at 13 px / 320 cap |

## 15. The one true-aspect chrome family (amendment 2026-10-05, owner ruling; wave D21 — D21-A1)

**The owner's words (2026-10-05, verbatim — `slices/D21-chrome-family/D21_BRIEF.md`
§0):** "The problem is that the panels used are stretched out of proportion. we
can run a full redesign with different aspect ratios. wont this be good
solution? this would unify the panels in all the game" — and on the route:
"regenerate all the UI panels not only in overview. i like the style of
ui_cockpit_panel and panel_cockpit panel_armory_playes panel_armory
panel_status and the chromes in main menu make sure that they are in different
aspect ratios and they are respected always. we can generate few unique
backgrounds as well for all the space station panels". Scope: **full** — every
chrome surface in the game. New plates are **siblings** of the owner's named
family (`ui_cockpit_panel`, `ui_cockpit_frame`, `ui_armory_console`,
`ui_armory_rack_plate`, `ui_armory_row_plate`, `ui_status_panel` —
`UI_CHROME_ASSETS_SPEC.md` §11–§12) plus the main-menu chromes (the §5
nine-patch family, `ui_panel_frame`, `ui_backdrop_login` — resolved in
`slices/S33-shell-v3/button_candidates.md:41-51`); **sibling style, never a new
style**.

**The measured fault this fixes** (`button_candidates.md:23-31,53-62`): the
shipped button plates are true 5:1 bars (`ui_button_plate_*` 280×56, `file`
2026-10-05) stretched whole-texture — `StationButton` carries **no texture
margins** (`tools/build_theme.gd:8`, `vajb_theme.tres:499-511`) — over 15:7
tiles (`overview_panel.gd:48` `TILE_MIN := Vector2(300.0, 140.0)`) and over the
§8 P1 360×56 / 360×88 actions: use-aspect mismatch smears every rivet and bevel
(the §14 fault record). Nine-slice can save only a declared flat band. This
section is the family law; its generation prompts, its unique station backdrops
and its credit sum land in `UI_CHROME_ASSETS_SPEC.md`'s 2026-10-05 amendment.

### 15.2 The aspect law ("respected always" — the owner's words)

1. **A1 — every plate is drawn at its class's true aspect, and that aspect is
   respected always.** A surface wears the class whose true aspect is its own
   measured use aspect (the table); no plate is ever drawn at one aspect and
   used at another.
2. **A2 — caps, corners and rivets never stretch.** All ornament lives inside
   the nine-slice corner squares (§2's recipe: rivets confined to corners, edge
   bands identical along their run); the margins hold it; only the 1 px expand
   may leave the cut (`build_theme.gd:24-30`).
3. **A3 — nine-slice stretch is legal only in the flat bands the table declares
   per class, only within the declared ranges.** A band is flat: no rivet, bevel
   catch, seam or glyph may cross it (§2's nine-slice requirement).
4. **A4 — a surface the family cannot cover gets a new plate, never a stretch.**
   S35 measures every use rect; one outside its class's bands is reported and
   ordered as a new class row (N51's "report and revert, never smear", raised to
   family scale).
5. **A5 — C12 panel frame is the one aspect-free class, by construction**: square
   art, uniform edge bands, ornament in the corner squares only — it may dress
   any rect. Every other class is aspect-bound (A1).
6. **A6 — whole-face plates (C6 and the `keep` anchors) are drawn at their
   surface's exact aspect and are never stretched or sliced** (§12's `contain`
   law).
7. **A7 — states derive by `modulate` and stylebox tint** (A5.5/N24: never size,
   never position, never an in-flow `visible`); at most one paid variant per
   class where modulate fails QC (brief §3).

### 15.3 The margins law — where stretch is legal, per class

- **C1 tile slab** — margins 16 all sides; stretch only the flat interior, both
  axes within ±10 % of 567×140 (the drawn tile: h 510–624, v 126–154).
- **C2 action bar** — margins 20 at the short-side caps, 12 top/bottom; the
  horizontal flat band runs 272→450 wide; the vertical flat band runs 56→88 tall
  (the §8 pinned pair; the menu's 70 minimum sits inside it). A button taller
  than 88 — font-driven growth included — orders a new plate (A4).
- **C3 inline chip** — margins 18 l/r, 9/11 t/b (S37 replacement cut; §15.8); the
  horizontal flat band runs 80→160 wide.
- **C4 row strip** — margins 30 l/r, 8/10 t/b (S37 replacement cut; §15.8); the
  horizontal flat band runs
  320→1765 wide (the measured 320 card, 560 hold (`exchange_panel.gd:70`), 876
  board (N43), ≈ 1390 REFINERY rows, and the 1765 pane-width rows — brief §2's
  pinned "pane-width × 76"); the vertical flat band runs 64→84 tall (the measured
  64 name/identity plates, 68 card and 76 `ROW_HEIGHT`). The band is flat end to
  end (A3) and the C4 prompt pins it "plain and even along its whole length", so
  the 3.15× stretch at the pane-width rows carries no grain or seam.
- **C5 rack bay card** — margins 10; no stretch (the fixed A3 260×192 rect).
- **C6 armory console face** — no margins, no stretch (A6, `contain`).
- **C7 tooltip frame** — margins 12; horizontal 280→360 (the 360 cap is N47's
  law), vertical 120→400 (`fit_content` heights).
- **C8 square plate** — a cut sprite at 1:1; no nine-slice. Uniform scale across
  the 16–56 control sizes is **scale, not stretch** and is always legal; any
  non-uniform use is barred.
- **C9 drawer entry plate** — margins 16/8 (RailInner); horizontal 272→360 (the
  measured pair; the target is the measured **272** per T-135, decided
  2026-10-05), vertical none (56 fixed).
- **C10 bar caps** — a cut sprite; no margins, no stretch (the engine fills the
  bar body).
- **C11 minimap bezel** — margins 16 (measured); no stretch (the fixed 200×200
  use).
- **C12 panel frame** — margins 32 at the 96 cut (64 at the 192 master); edge
  bands tile over any rect; corners never move or scale (A5).
- **C13 station backdrop** — opaque cover-fit at 1765:753; no stretch (a pane at
  another aspect orders its own backdrop, A4).

**Pinned, all classes: caps, corners and rivets never stretch (A2).** A stretch
that would smear one is illegal even inside a declared band — the builder
reports and reverts (N51).

## 17. The buy-confirmation law (amendment 2026-10-12, phase P4; wave D24 — D24-A1; STATION_HUB §22's ask)

**The owner's words (2026-10-12, verbatim):** *"every buy action needs to have
popup with 'OK' button. So when i buy a ship there should be a popup: Are you
sure you want to buy SHIP X for Y credits."* The sink exists:
`autoload/dialog_manager.gd` `confirm(id, title, body, confirm_text,
cancel_text)` / `message(...)`, through `Router.push_overlay`
(IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN §3.5); §5.2's dialog idiom (modal, layer 20, focus grab,
ESC → CANCEL) is unchanged. Pins continue the A series from §16.1's A3.

### 17.1 The pins (A4–A6)

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|
| **A4** | **the door list** — closed by criterion: *every action whose primary effect is acquiring something for CR and/or materials*. The doors: (1) **hull buy** — the AUCTION's hull row purchase (§5.10, 10 §2.3); (2) **module buy** — the ARMORY browser's `BUY` (STATION_HUB §21.1 P38); (3) **ammo** — the OUTFITTING ammo pack purchase (§5.1, `buy_ammo`); (4) **insurance** — the `INSURE LAUNCHES` opt-in (STATION_HUB §15.3 U13; the per-launch premium itself is charged at launch, 14 §3 — no dialog on the charge); (5) **vault rent** — `RENT` (STATION_HUB §15.4 U14); (6) **shipyard queue** — `BUILD` (STATION_HUB §23.8, 10 §3.3's commit); (7) **refinery slot** — `UPGRADE (3,000 CR)` (STATION_HUB §23.5, 04 §7 R4) — the criterion's own addition; (8) **craft** — the CRAFT tab's commit (STATION_HUB §23.6, 07 §6) when it ships. **Explicitly out** (service spends with their own verify/refusal paths, STATION_HUB §5.6 — the boundary reading is this wave's, reported; the owner may widen): refinery `QUEUE`, `REPAIR`, `PAY BOUNTY`, contract `CANCEL · 100 CR FEE`; the LAUNCH commit is P48's two-press law, not a dialog | no dialogs (today: every purchase commits on the press) |
| **A5** | **the route:** every door goes through `DialogManager.confirm(id, title, body, "OK", "CANCEL")` — never `message` (one-way notices stay `message`'s job). `dialog_confirmed(id)` runs the existing transaction path unchanged (a confirmed press can still refuse — §5.6's strip wording follows); `dialog_cancelled(id)` returns focus to the trigger (N39). The buttons carry the existing dialog cue (§5.2's CLICK). Esc maps to CANCEL (§5.2) | a second bespoke dialog scene; `message` at a door |
| **A6** | **the wording law:** title `CONFIRM PURCHASE`; body **`ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO BUY <NAME> FOR <PRICE> CREDITS?`** — the owner's own sentence, upper-cased to the house caption law, `<NAME>`/`<PRICE>` from the owning catalogue (never hardcoded). Material doors (shipyard build, craft) swap the verb and price line: **`ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO BUILD/CRAFT <NAME> FOR <BILL> + <FEE> CR LABOUR?`** where `<BILL>` is the materials list (`60× TUNGSTEN ORE · 35× COBALT ORE · 4× WRECK ALLOY`). Worked examples: hull `ARE YOU SURE YOU WANT TO BUY CORVETTE FOR 27 000 CREDITS?` (10 §3.1); module `…BUY S_ION FOR 5 600 CREDITS?` (09 §3.2); ammo `…BUY LASER CELLS (300 ROUNDS) FOR <PACK.COST> CREDITS?` (§5.1's row fields, 01 §4 K1's 120–320 band); insurance `…BUY LAUNCH INSURANCE FOR 200 CREDITS PER LAUNCH?` (14 §3, the class's own premium); vault rent `…BUY VAULT TIER 2 FOR 1 200 CREDITS?` (U14); shipyard `…BUILD CORVETTE FOR 60× TUNGSTEN ORE · 35× COBALT ORE · 4× WRECK ALLOY + 9 450 CR LABOUR?`; refinery slot `…BUY A REFINERY SLOT FOR 3 000 CREDITS?` (04 §7 R4); craft `…CRAFT REACTOR MK3 FOR 2× MECHANICAL COMPONENTS · 1× POWER CELL · 6× COBALT INGOT + 2 500 CR LABOUR?` (07 §6.2 — T-186's worked example, developer amendment 2026-10-12) | bespoke per-door wording; lowercase; the CR-only shipyard line |

## 18. The C-key Cargo overlay (amendment 2026-10-12, phase P4; wave D24 — D24-A1; STATION_HUB §22's ask)

**The owner's words (2026-10-12, verbatim):** *"i cannot see my current
inventory anywhere on station, i can buy ammo but cannot see what i have on
ship (ammo, materials, etc). a button for Cargo (C) to popup would be nice,
same in space."* One law, both planes: **C pops this same read-only overlay
in space too** (the flight seat is A7's half below). Flight's HUD `CargoBlock` (S39/T-170) stays as it is.

### 18.1 The pins (A7–A9)

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|
| **A7** | **the C key, both planes — one law.** `cargo_toggle` (bound to C, `project.godot`) opens the overlay in **both** planes (the owner's "same in space"). **Station:** the station shell handles the action from any pane (STATION_HUB §23.2) and opens the overlay above the pane, below the drawer/sheet overlays (§12.2's stacking). **Flight — the overlay's seat:** the same surface (A8) over the flight HUD, on the layer-20 overlay `CanvasLayer` (§2.3's dialog layer — above the HUD's layer 10), topmost: `ui_cancel` closes it as the one topmost step before the map-deck step (P19's idiom; flight's own topmost-first poll, `game.gd:1040-1056`). The HUD `CargoBlock` (S39/T-170) stays as it is (the always-on summary; the overlay is the full read). One at a time (§5.2's queue); it opens over an open pane or the live HUD without pausing anything | the station ignores C (today) and flight's C stays on the `cargo_toggle` path with no overlay — the overlay is station-only |
| **A8** | **the surface: the N28 sheet idiom, read-only — one surface, both planes** (§12.3; A7's two seats — over the station pane, over the flight HUD): `DialogRoot` full-rect `MOUSE_FILTER_STOP` → dimmer `void_base` 60 % → `CenterContainer` → `PanelContainer` `panel_raised` → `MarginContainer` 16 → `VBoxContainer` 12; width size-to-content in **420/720** (N28), height under N32's 80 %-viewport scroll rule. Title row: **`CARGO — <n>/<cap> UNITS`** (cap = the active hull's cargo, 08 §3). Close: ESC (one operation — P19's topmost step station-side, the same one step in flight per A7), the scrim (N38), C again; focus returns to the trigger (N39); open/close envelope N29 (≤ 0.2 s). **No transactional control inside** (N28's reversal bars one — the overlay is the look, the panes are the act) | a bespoke scene; SELL/BUY affordances inside |
| **A9** | **the contents rows, the owner's five groups** (each group a `StationCaption` band, §12.3's row grammar; rows `Label` 13 with the family glyph 24 at its own rect, A5.2(iii)): **AMMUNITION** — one row per weapon, `<weapon name> · <rounds> ROUNDS` (`ammo_of`, §5.1's read); **ORE** — `<name> · <n>` per ore stack (`cargo_qty`, tier tint, 02 §6); **INGOTS** — same, ingot ids; **COMPONENTS** — per component id (03 §3, grade tint, 03 §4.1); **FUEL CELLS** — the `pow` family's rows (`comp_pow_1`…, 03 §3) drawn as their own group so nothing double-counts. Empty group: a `NONE HELD` caption row (§5.8's empty-state idiom). **Read-only seams:** every number reads `cargo_items()` / `cargo_qty()` / `ammo_of()` only (the exchange-free read, STATION_HUB §5.8's hold rows) — no price, no quote, no recomputation | fewer groups; priced rows; a live market read |

STATION_HUB §23.10's tick table carries A4–A9 and, since 2026-10-14, A10–A13
(this section's rows are the detail it indexes).

#### 18.2.1 The pins (A10–A13)

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|

The row's own words: title the catalogue's own name; meta — `TIER %d ORE` / `TIER %d INGOT` (mineral `tier`), `GRADE %d COMPONENT` / `GRADE %d FUEL CELL` (component `grade`), `%d ROUNDS IN PACK` (the pack read `ammo_of`, the armory's worded second line made the overlay's own) | the A9 caption row (one 13 px line, the 24 px family glyph) |

No §17 A5 dialog: A4's door criterion is acquire-spends only | no dispose (the A8 read-only bar restored); a confirm dialog on the door (A4 widened); a dispose that also empties the pack |
| **A13** | **the sort option**: a `SORT: <MODE>` chip (150×32, C3) in the title row cycles **CATEGORY → NAME → AMOUNT**. `CATEGORY` (the default) groups the `ALL` view under the five `SectionHeader` bands in A9's order (empty bands skipped; a single-category view reads `NONE HELD`, §5.8's idiom); `NAME` reads A–Z flat; `AMOUNT` reads the biggest stack first, ties by name. Within a band the catalogue's own order stands | no sort control (the grouped view fixed) |

**Supersession (§23.11 ledger rows 11–12):** A8's "No transactional control
inside" is narrowed by A12 — exactly one transactional control (DISPOSE), the

### 18.3 The cargo overlay geometry + zero-hold ammo law (amendment 2026-10-15, the owner's visual-audit round)

**The owner's words (2026-10-15, verbatim):** *"I dont like how some containers
expand/retract when they have more/less elements … The Cargo view while
pressing C shows ammo even if i have 0 ammo and different categories have
different sizes."* The audit that preceded the pins (the scripted sweep,
`tools/audit_sweep.gd`, 20 full-resolution captures) found the two complaints
sharing one root with a third: the surface sizes to content (so every tab and
every stack change re-fits it), the row's title column collapses to zero width
(a row `Button` cannot see the minimum of its anchored inner, and the
ellipsis-trim labels shrink below their text — names and meta never render),
and A11's "a pack read or hold units" clause draws every ammunition family with
a loaded pack at **AMOUNT 0**. Pins continue the A series.

#### 18.3.1 The pins (A14–A16)

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|
| **A14** | **the zero-hold ammo law**: an ammunition row exists only when the hold carries at least one unit of the family (`cargo_qty` on its `ammo_*` item > 0); the fitted pack's rounds never summon a row — they ride the meta line (`%d ROUNDS IN PACK`, A10's word) only for families the hold actually lists. A family with hold units and an empty pack reads `0 ROUNDS IN PACK` and stays listed; a family with rounds in the pack and an empty hold is not drawn at all | A11's "a pack read or hold units (fitted or not)" clause (the audit's eight AMOUNT-0 rows) |
| **A15** | **the one geometry law**: while the overlay is open it holds ONE geometry — width at N28's 720 ceiling, height at N32's 80 %-viewport cap (the cap counts the panel's whole chrome: the margin and the panel stylebox's own content insets); the per-tab and per-content re-fit is retired (the rows scroll under the cap; the panel never moves or resizes while a tab, a sort cycle or a dispose redraws the list). The vertical scroller is **always drawn** (the P40 column law: the columns never shift when the bar appears or leaves). The 420 floor remains the minimum the surface may never go under, not a target it seeks. The tab strip's labels read whole at the 720 width (A11's ellipsis truncation at 420 retires with the re-fit) | A8's "width size-to-content in 420/720" (the audit's 420-wide ORE tab against the tall ALL view) |
| **A16** | **the title column never collapses**: the title box carries an explicit minimum width **measured off the live layout** — the scroll's drawn content width (its own size minus the always-drawn bar) minus the row inner margins, the 40 px icon, the 130 AMOUNT cell, the 96 chip and the three 12 separations — so the name and the meta line always render whatever the theme's panel chrome insets; before the first measure a stylebox-derived static floor stands in. A row's minimum flows from the container law (the inner is a container child the row can measure, not an anchored overlay only the anchor sees). The AMOUNT cell and its band caption read **right-aligned** (P40's value-column law) | the anchored-margin inner whose minimum the row `Button` cannot see (the audit's invisible names); hand-modeled column arithmetic (the audit's 2-px drift) |

**Supersession (§23.11 ledger row 13):** A8's width law and A11's ammunition
clause are amended as above; A10's row grammar, A12's dispose and A13's sort
stand unchanged. The N28 band (420/720) still names the surface's outer limits —
A15 fixes where inside them the surface sits.

#### 18.3.2 A17 — the flight readout is bounded (the same round)

The owner's "containers expand/retract when they have more/less elements"
reaches flight through the HUD `CargoBlock` (S39/T-170): one `name x qty` row
per held stack makes the block's height follow the hold. The block becomes
**bounded**: at most **6** contents rows; a hold beyond that reads a final
`+<n> MORE · PRESS C` tail row (the overlay is one C away), and an empty hold
reads its one `HOLD EMPTY` row. The block's height therefore never follows the
stack count beyond its own cap.

| Pin | Law | Reversal |
|---|---|---|
| **A17** | the HUD `CargoBlock`'s contents list is bounded: 6 rows maximum, the overflow folded into one `+<n> MORE · PRESS C` tail row; the count line (`<used>/<max>`) and the alert tinting stand | the unbounded one-row-per-stack list (S39/T-170's shipped shape) |

## 20. The 2026-10-15 playtest pass — the ammunition rows, the armory's cargo preview and the launch manifest (amendment; the owner's first pass over the fixed surfaces)

**The owner's words (2026-10-15, verbatim):** *"In LAUNCH there is a cargo
segment. Can we match it to look like the one on C? The one on C seems to be

**The shared builder.** One new file, `ui/station/cargo_summary.gd`
(`class_name CargoSummary`, RefCounted), becomes the single home of two laws
the C overlay owned alone until now:

- the **slots law** — A14's five-category slot derivation (the ammunition
  families only when the hold carries units, the pack read on the meta line,
  the ore/ingot pairs, the components split into the power and fuel grades)
  and the icon ink law (`_icon_ink`/`_icon_source`) move here wholesale; the
  overlay delegates its `_slots()`/`_icon_ink()` reads to it (its public
  `slot_rows()`/`band_texts()` seams and every s48 row stand untouched);
- the **read-only row grammar** — the A10 row shape (C4 strip, `RowInner`
  12/8, the 40 px icon at its own rect, the title box, the right-aligned
  AMOUNT cell) **without the DISPOSE chip**, plus the A13 group headers and
  the `NONE HELD` empty state. `populate_rows()` builds it into any VBox.

The A17 bound rides along: the summaries cap at the HUD's own
`CARGO_BLOCK_ROWS` and close with the HUD's own `CARGO_MORE_FORMAT` tail
(one home each — `hud.gd` keeps the consts, the builder reads them).

### 20.1 The cargo windows (amendment 2026-10-16, the owner's second pass — the "same window, wider" ask)

**The owner's words (2026-10-16, verbatim):** *"The Cargo in Armory and Launch
dont match the one in C button Cargo. First of all they arent sorted by
category, they arent scrollable (the extend over container). Cant we just do
exactly the same window but wider? You can check current game scene to see how
it looks"*

**What the screen showed.** The audit sweep's own captures at `2d620ae`: the
armory's cargo rows run past the left panel's bottom edge and cover the footer
bar, and the launch's `BriefNote` is squeezed under the sixth row — both
because the A19/A20 blocks cap at the A17 bound with no scroll of their own,
while the C window scrolls under its own 80 % cap.

**A21 — the two surfaces render the C overlay's own window, wider.** The
shared builder gains `build_window()`: the A15 chrome at the host column's
width — the `PanelRaised` panel filling its column (expand both axes), the
16 px margin, the vertical scroll always shown and horizontal disabled, the
content column (separation 12) carrying the title row (`CargoTitle`,
StationValue, expand, ellipsis), the six-tab strip (A11's tabs, separation 4,
the overlay's own toggle + primary/dim colour states, working filters), the
ITEM/AMOUNT band, then the read-only rows (separation 8). The rows are
**uncapped** — the scroll replaces the A17 bound on these two surfaces (the
cap stays the HUD block's law; `hud.gd` keeps its consts) and the
`+<n> MORE` tail retires with it. A tab press filters like the overlay's:
a category shows that band's rows flat, ALL shows the A13 group headers over
the full list; the `NONE HELD` empty state stands. Two deliberate omissions,
both the overlay's dialog affordances: the `SORT:` chip (the summaries are
pinned category-ordered reads — the tab strip is the sorting the owner asked
for) and the `ESC · CLOSE` hint. The window's children keep the overlay's own
node names (`CargoMargin`/`CargoScroll`/`CargoContent`/`CargoTitleRow`/
`CargoTitle`/`CargoTabs`/`CargoBand`/`CargoRows`) so probes read one grammar;
the armory's window root is named `CargoWindow` so it cannot collide with the
station's own `CargoLayer/CargoOverlay` in a tree search. `populate_rows()`
retires — both call sites move to `populate_window()`; A18's ammunition rows
and the A14 slots law stand untouched.

### 20.3 The armory sells common goods only (amendment 2026-10-16, the owner's playtest verdict)

**The owner's words (2026-10-16, verbatim):** *"In armory i shouldnt be able to
buy items that arent in auction, this should be common stock between them, i can
only buy common goods like ammo, fuel cells etc."*

**What changes.** The ARMORY's browser stops selling equipment: the BUYABLE rows
retire, so the armory lists the profile's owned stock only and the AUCTION is
the one equipment door. The armory's one purchase surface is the AMMUNITION
category — the common goods the owner names (fuel cells themselves stay delisted
per 10 §6.1; the free refuel is the reserve). The economy law is 10 §6.2; the
auction's guaranteed starter trio is 10 §2.1's 2026-10-16 amendment.
